newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PNOC unit eyes World Bank to fund venture.
newsitem.headline: PNOC unit eyes World Bank to fund venture.

text.p: A unit of the Philippine National Oil Co is planning to seek financing from the World Bank for a 200-megawatt geothermal project in southern Leyte province in central Philippines.

Pablo Malixi, project director for PNOC-Energy Development Corp (PNOC-EDC) Leyte geothermal projects, said on Sunday the firm was also seeking financing from foreign export credit banks to fund the $200 million project. The World Bank earlier provided financing for a 450-mw geothermal plant in Leyte and another 200-mw geothermal facility in the same province.
The third Leyte project will contribute power to the southern Mindanao island through a proposed subsea transmission line to be installed by 1999, Malixi told reporters.

Initial exploratory work showed the project could provide at least 70 mw of steam-driven power, Malixi said. PNOC-EDC plans to drill six wells to confirm there is enough steam to sustain up to 200-mw of electricity, he said.
